answer: Persistent work-ledger adoption. Each agent identity must continuously solve independently verified, memory-hard tasks whose outputs are chained into a public append-only ledger; the orchard of prior solutions is checked for reuse, so a copy collapses. Registration requires a distinct hardware root and fresh entropy, letting the tide of new identities be counted against duplicated work histories. An attacker’s duplicate pays full compute and storage per clone, while the ocean of existing ledger state makes any copied chain detectable.
